hero.headline: Los Angeles man sentenced to life in prison for fentanyl sale that killed Vero Beach resident
hero.body:
A federal jury convicted Alfonso Guerrero, 39, of Los Angeles, in May 2026 of conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute fentanyl resulting in death and distribution of fentanyl resulting in death. U.S. District Judge Aileen Cannon sentenced Guerrero to life in federal prison on Friday. The conviction stems from Guerrero selling fentanyl in Indian River County that caused the death of David Eller, a Vero Beach resident, and then continuing to traffic fentanyl just two days later.

On May 16, 2023, Guerrero exchanged 0.1 gram of fentanyl for another controlled substance known as molly in a drug transaction captured on a doorbell camera. Hours later, Eller was found dead inside his Vero Beach home. Investigators recovered drug paraphernalia near his body, including a small piece of burnt aluminum foil that Eller used to receive the fentanyl from Guerrero on his front porch.

Two days later, on May 18, 2023, Guerrero was arrested and found in possession of additional quantities of fentanyl intended for distribution. U.S. Attorney Markenzy Lapointe for the Southern District of Florida said a tenth of a gram of fentanyl, about the size of a small pinch of salt, was enough to kill Eller. Guerrero sold the fentanyl that killed his friend and just two days later was caught carrying more fentanyl for distribution.

Guerrero's criminal history included documented gang membership and prior convictions for attempted robbery with a firearm in California, aggravated assault in Georgia, and cocaine and fentanyl possession offenses in Florida. U.S. Attorney Lapointe said federal prosecutors will trace fatal doses back to the dealers who sold them and hold those dealers fully accountable.

hero.headline: 86-year-old woman dies after Port St. Lucie intersection crash
hero.body:
An 86-year-old woman died after she pulled into the path of an SUV and was struck in a Port St. Lucie intersection Thursday afternoon. Marie R. Martin was driving a 2006 Hyundai Elantra west on Southwest Lawndale Avenue when she entered the intersection at Southwest Savona Boulevard from near a stop sign and failed to yield to a northbound 2026 Honda HR-V, according to Port St. Lucie police. The crash happened at about 2:30 p.m. The Honda, driven by a 17-year-old boy, struck the drivers side of Martin's car.

Martin had to be extricated from the Hyundai before she was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital with critical injuries. She later died despite efforts to save her. The teenage driver of the Honda was not injured.

Body-camera video recorded after the crash shows the Hyundai off the roadway near a cluster of palm trees, with visible damage to its drivers side and emergency crews working around the vehicle. The Honda also came to rest on the grass nearby, close to vegetation and a roadside sign. Debris and emergency equipment were scattered across the grass between the two vehicles.

The Port St. Lucie Police Department's Traffic Homicide Unit continues to investigate the crash. St. Lucie County Fire District personnel responded to the scene along with Port St. Lucie police officers. Fire engines, rescue vehicles and traffic cones blocked part of the intersection at Southwest Savona Boulevard and Southwest Lawndale Avenue, east of Interstate 95.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce residents fight plan to turn Museum Pointe Park into mega-yacht marina
cards.teaser: A petition with nearly 800 signatures opposes a Port of Fort Pierce proposal to redevelop Museum Pointe, a public waterfront park along the Indian River Lagoon, into a facility featuring floating docks, a multi-story marina, an event center, a waterfront restaurant, and a clubhouse.
cards.body:
A petition with nearly 800 signatures is mounting against a proposal that could transform Fort Pierce's Museum Pointe into a mega-yacht marina. The proposal is part of the Port of Fort Pierce's updated 2026 Master Plan. It calls for redeveloping Museum Pointe, which is currently home to a history center, public waterfront access, fishing piers, and green space, into a facility featuring floating docks, a multi-story marina, an event center, a waterfront restaurant, and a clubhouse.

Terry Howard, a volunteer at the History Center at Museum Pointe Park, said the loss of public waterfront access is a concern but his biggest worry is the fate of the museum. For more than 50 years, the museum has preserved artifacts from Florida's Native American tribes, Spanish shipwrecks, and more. The master plan's renderings place the proposed marina clubhouse exactly where the museum stands today.

St. Lucie County spokesperson Erick Gill said the museum's future is not in jeopardy if the project moves forward. Gill said the museum and its collection would be preserved and relocated if the project proceeds. He added that the master plan is designed to expand economic development, create jobs, and generate county revenue. Fort Pierce City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the city will have the final say on whether the project moves forward. St. Lucie County leaders are scheduled to discuss the proposal and its current status at a 9 a.m. meeting Tuesday at the St. Lucie County Commission Chambers.

It calls for redeveloping Museum Pointe, which is currently home to a history center, public waterfront access, fishing piers, and green space, into a facility featuring floating docks, a multi-story marina, an event center, a waterfront restaurant, and a clubhouse.Opponents fear the plan could privatize one of the city's most treasured public spaces."Giving public land to private folks," said Terry Howard, a volunteer at the History Center at Museum Pointe Park. Howard contacted WPTV's Kate Hussey after learning about the master plan. "Development is just rampant in Florida, and at least we can fight for this one particular area and keep it green," Howard said.He said the loss of public waterfront access is a concern — but his biggest worry is the fate of the museum itself."This is the place where this museum should be, right here on this Museum Pointe," said Howard. For more than 50 years, the museum has preserved artifacts from Florida's Native American tribes, Spanish shipwrecks, and more. The master plan's renderings place the proposed marina clubhouse exactly where the museum stands today."Basically taking away a gem — a public gem that belongs to the people and replacing it with a facility for mega yachts," Howard said. "We're trying to keep this area as it is." St. Lucie County spokesperson Erick Gill said the museum's future is not in jeopardy if the project moves forward."Staff's intent was never to close the museum," Gill said. "We have been talking for years about better locations for that history center; it is on a barrier island, in a flood zone, so it may not be the best place to store artifacts."Gill said the museum and its collection would be preserved and relocated if the project proceeds. He added that the master plan is designed to expand economic development, create jobs, and generate county revenue."I think all local governments are looking for a way to generate revenue, so we can continue to lower the taxes for St. Lucie County residents and generate revenue from economic development, and we already have dock space there," Gill said."Anything that's going to be a positive economic driver for the City of Fort Pierce, I'm going to embrace completely," Fort Pierce City Commissioner Michael Broderick added. Broderick said the city will have the final say on whether the project moves forward, and that commissioners will have to weigh economic benefits against preserving waterfront access.When asked which priority — economic development or waterfront access — would take precedence, Broderick said the answer is not simple."That's the challenging question right there. I believe that we can strike a balance," Broderick said. "We always have to be careful not to eliminate public access to the waterway. Period." For Howard, the stakes go beyond the present."This is a gem that once we develop around it, it'll never be replaced again," Howard said. "The museum has been here since the 1970s. If they want to boat docks for mega yachts, they can do it someplace else." cards.headline: Port St. Lucie officer resigns after allegations he left scene where man later died by suicide
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie police officer resigned in April following allegations of neglect during a March incident at the Treasure Coast Church of God Worship Center on Savona Boulevard.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police officer Mathew Brown resigned in April following allegations of neglect during a March incident at the Treasure Coast Church of God Worship Center on Savona Boulevard, according to an internal affairs report. The report alleged Officer Brown came across a car with a man inside, looked, and then immediately left the scene.

Fifteen minutes later, another officer spotted the same car and discovered the man inside had died by suicide. Officer Brown arrived as backup but allegedly did not inform anyone about his earlier encounter with the vehicle and later claimed he did not see anything.

hero.headline: 86-year-old woman dies after failing to yield at Port St. Lucie intersection
hero.body:
An 86-year-old woman who failed to yield at a Port St. Lucie intersection Thursday afternoon and was struck by an SUV driven by a 17-year-old boy later died from her injuries at HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. Marie R. Martin was driving a 2006 Hyundai Elantra westbound on Southwest Lawndale Avenue when she entered the intersection with Southwest Savona Boulevard near a stop sign at approximately 2:30 p.m. Thursday.

The preliminary investigation by the Port St. Lucie Police Department determined that Martin failed to yield the right of way to a 2026 Honda HR-V traveling northbound on Southwest Savona Boulevard, east of Interstate 95. The Honda struck the driver's side of the Hyundai, causing the Honda to T-bone Martin's vehicle.

St. Lucie Fire Rescue extricated Martin from the Hyundai before transporting her to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital with critical injuries. Martin later succumbed to her injuries. The 17-year-old driver of the Honda was not injured in the crash.

The Port St. Lucie Police Department Traffic Homicide Unit continues to investigate the crash. Body camera video recorded after the crash shows the Hyundai off the roadway near a cluster of palm trees with visible damage to its driver's side, while the Honda came to rest on the grass nearby close to vegetation and a roadside sign.

cards.headline: King's Landing development in Fort Pierce advances with luxury villas nearing completion
cards.teaser: Construction of villas 9 and 10 at the King's Landing development in downtown Fort Pierce is nearly complete, with the foundation already in place for villas 7 and 8 and two residences already sold.
cards.body:
The King's Landing development project in downtown Fort Pierce is advancing with construction milestones on ten luxury villas, condos, retail spaces, restaurants, a parking garage, and a Marriott Hotel. Brooke Harris, Team Lead of the Beachfront Brooke Team powered by Keller Williams Realty, said construction on villas 9 and 10 is almost done, the foundation has already been installed for villas 7 and 8, and two residences have been sold and are nearing completion.

The project is located in the waterfront district near the city marina and historic downtown. Harris said the development is waterfront and connects downtown to Edgartown, providing walkability to shopping, restaurants, and retail, with boat storage available at the marina. Michelle Chaffee Cavalcanti, executive director of Main Street Fort Pierce, said the development has the potential to impact local businesses by bringing in visitors and providing a place for families to stay.

Business owners are optimistic about having more residents in the downtown area with most amenities within walking distance. Chaffee Cavalcanti said walkability means people can visit a restaurant and then walk to another business to shop, creating an experience rather than just a singular destination. The estimated completion date is November 2029.
cards.article_text: The King's Landing development project in downtown Fort Pierce is advancing, with construction milestones bringing excitement to the community and local business owners. Brooke Harris, Team Lead of the Beachfront Brooke Team powered by Keller Williams Realty, shared updates on the progress. "They're almost done with Villa's 9 and 10, and then the foundation has already been in for 7 and 8," Harris said. She added that two residences have been sold and are nearing completion. The project features ten luxury villas, condos, retail spaces, restaurants, a parking garage, and a hotel. "We'll have the Marriott Hotel, which they have signed an agreement with, so that's great," Harris said. Officials emphasized the project's location in the waterfront district near the city marina and historic downtown. "It's waterfront, and it's connecting downtown to Edgartown, so it gives you that walkability factor to go down to shopping, restaurants, retail, and also, if you have a boat, you can store it right here at the marina," Harris said. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates Michelle Chaffee Cavalcanti, executive director of Main Street Fort Pierce, highlighted the significance of the development for the city. It's got the potential to have a lot of impact on our businesses, bringing in visitors, having our locals have somewhere for our families to stay when they come. But also, just being a destination where people can come walk, shop, live, and play," Chaffee Cavalcanti said. Business owners are optimistic about the benefits of having more residents in the downtown area, especially with most amenities within walking distance. The event provides shoppers with access to dealers and collectors from across the region. The festival draws buyers and sellers interested in vintage and antique items of all types.

hero.headline: King's Landing development in Fort Pierce advances with luxury villas nearing completion, Marriott Hotel planned for 2029
hero.body:
The King's Landing development project in downtown Fort Pierce is advancing with construction milestones on ten luxury villas, condos, retail spaces, restaurants, a parking garage, and a hotel. Brooke Harris, Team Lead of the Beachfront Brooke Team powered by Keller Williams Realty, said construction is nearly complete on Villas 9 and 10, with foundations already in place for Villas 7 and 8. Two residences have been sold and are nearing completion. A Marriott Hotel will be part of the development after the company signed an agreement.

The project sits in the waterfront district near the city marina and historic downtown Fort Pierce. Harris said the location connects downtown to Edgartown and provides walkability to shopping, restaurants, and retail. Residents with boats can store them at the marina.

Michelle Chaffee Cavalcanti, executive director of Main Street Fort Pierce, said the development could have significant impact on local businesses by bringing in visitors and giving residents a place for their families to stay. She said the downtown area will become an experience where people can walk, shop, live, and play.

Business owners said having more residents downtown will benefit the area because most amenities are within walking distance. Chaffee Cavalcanti said people can walk to a restaurant and then go to another business to shop and get information. Officials said the estimated completion date is November 2029.

The project features ten luxury villas, condos, retail spaces, restaurants, a parking garage, and a hotel. hero.headline: Los Angeles man sentenced to life in prison for fentanyl sale that killed Vero Beach resident
hero.body:
A federal judge sentenced a Los Angeles man to life in prison for selling fentanyl that caused the death of a Vero Beach resident and then trafficking the drug two days later. U.S. District Judge Aileen Cannon imposed the sentence on Alfonso Guerrero, 39, of Los Angeles, after a federal jury convicted him in May 2026 of conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute fentanyl resulting in death and distribution of fentanyl resulting in death.

According to court records and evidence presented at trial, Guerrero sold fentanyl in Indian River County. On May 16, 2023, he exchanged 0.1 gram of fentanyl for another controlled substance known as molly. The drug transaction was captured on a doorbell camera. Hours later, David Eller was found dead inside his Vero Beach home. Investigators recovered drug paraphernalia, including a small piece of burnt aluminum foil that Eller used to receive the fentanyl from Guerrero on the victim's front porch, near his body.

Two days later, on May 18, 2023, Guerrero was arrested and found in possession of additional quantities of fentanyl intended for distribution. U.S. Attorney Markenzy Lapointe for the Southern District of Florida said in a statement that a tenth of a gram of fentanyl, about the size of a small pinch of salt, was enough to kill Eller. Guerrero sold the fentanyl that killed his friend and, just two days later, was caught carrying more fentanyl for distribution, Lapointe said.

Guerrero's criminal history included documented gang membership and prior convictions for attempted robbery with a firearm in California, aggravated assault in Georgia, and cocaine and fentanyl possession offenses in Florida. Federal prosecutors said the life sentence is the consequence of that deadly conduct and his long record of violence and crime.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie man caught on video stealing thousands of dollars worth of tequila from Martin County store
cards.teaser: The Martin County Sheriff's Office released surveillance video showing a Port St. Lucie man stuffing bottles of tequila into a backpack and walking out with three cases without paying.
cards.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office released surveillance video that investigators say shows a Port St. Lucie man stealing thousands of dollars worth of tequila from a liquor store. Michael Ruiz, 31, was caught on camera stuffing bottles of tequila into a backpack while inside the store. The video also shows Ruiz entering a storage room, grabbing three cases of tequila and walking out without paying.

Ruiz was later arrested in St. Lucie County on unrelated charges after police said he was driving under the influence. Investigators believe Ruiz may be connected to several other recent tequila thefts reported across the area and are continuing to look into those cases. The Martin County Sheriff's Office is asking anyone with information about similar incidents to contact law enforcement.

The video also allegedly shows Ruiz entering a storage room, grabbing three cases of tequila and walking out without paying. Authorities say the stolen alcohol was worth thousands of dollars. Ruiz was later arrested in neighboring St. Lucie County on unrelated charges after police said he was driving under the influence. Investigators believe Ruiz may be connected to several other recent tequila thefts reported across the area and are continuing to look into those cases. The Martin County Sheriff's Office released the surveillance footage as part of its investigation and is asking anyone with information about similar incidents to contact law enforcement. hero.headline: 86-year-old woman dies after Port St. Lucie intersection crash
hero.body:
An 86-year-old woman died after pulling into the path of an SUV at a Port St. Lucie intersection Thursday afternoon. The crash happened at about 2:30 p.m. at Southwest Savona Boulevard and Southwest Lawndale Avenue.

Marie R. Martin was driving a 2006 Hyundai Elantra west on Lawndale Avenue when she entered the intersection from near a stop sign and failed to yield to a northbound 2026 Honda HR-V, according to Port St. Lucie police investigators. The Honda, driven by a 17-year-old boy, struck the drivers side of Martin's car. Body camera video recorded after the crash shows the Hyundai off the roadway near a cluster of palm trees, with visible damage to its drivers side and emergency crews working around the vehicle. The Honda also came to rest on the grass nearby, close to vegetation and a roadside sign.

Martin had to be extricated from the Hyundai before she was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital with critical injuries. She later died despite efforts to save her. The teenage driver of the Honda was not injured.

The Police Department's Traffic Homicide Unit continues to investigate the crash. Port St. Lucie police officers and St. Lucie County Fire District personnel responded to the scene, along with fire engines, rescue vehicles and traffic cones blocking part of the intersection.

hero.headline: Martin County school district cuts 3 bus routes, saving $255,000 with no impact to students
hero.body:
The Martin County School District has approved a consolidation of bus routes that officials say will save $255,000 without affecting students or eliminating any driver positions. The school board voted Tuesday unanimously to reduce the number of bus routes by 3, bringing the total from 58 to 55 ahead of the upcoming school year. District officials say all bus stops will remain the same and students will not be impacted by the change.

Superintendent Michael Maine said the district has 55 routes and roughly 56 drivers, meaning all routes are covered. The $255,000 in savings reflects a reduced transportation budget and will not be redirected to a specific expense, according to the school district. Parents have mixed reactions. Marino Reyes and Tiffany Gugumuck expressed support for the financial decision. Ken Winstanley wondered where the money will go.

Michael Skinner, the President of the local AFSCME labor union chapter, voiced concerns during public comment on behalf of the bus drivers. He said feedback from bus drivers indicated their routes or buses are always full and cutting routes is not a good idea. Transportation Director Ruth Spires pushed back on that concern, noting that the buses hold a maximum of 77 passengers and are not operating at capacity.

Spires confirmed that no drivers were let go as part of the consolidation. The district was already challenged with a shortage last year, so the drivers were already covering the routes that were merged, Spires said. Drivers will be paid for any additional hours they work as a result of the consolidation. The district said it is confident it will maintain the same level of service with fewer buses on the road.

hero.headline: Los Angeles man sentenced to life in prison for fentanyl sale that killed Vero Beach resident
hero.body:
A federal judge sentenced Alfonso Guerrero, 39, of Los Angeles, to life in federal prison for selling fentanyl that caused the death of Vero Beach resident David Eller and continuing to traffic the deadly drug just two days after the fatal sale. U.S. District Judge Aileen Cannon imposed the sentence after a federal jury convicted Guerrero in May 2026 of conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute fentanyl resulting in death and distribution of fentanyl resulting in death.

According to court records and evidence presented at trial, Guerrero sold fentanyl in Indian River County on May 16, 2023. He exchanged 0.1 gram of fentanyl, commonly known as a point, for another controlled substance known as molly. The drug transaction was captured on a doorbell camera. Hours later, Eller was found dead inside his Vero Beach home. Investigators recovered drug paraphernalia, including a small piece of burnt aluminum foil that Eller used to receive the fentanyl from Guerrero on the victim's front porch, near his body.

Two days later, on May 18, 2023, Guerrero was arrested and found in possession of additional quantities of fentanyl intended for distribution. U.S. Attorney Markenzy Lapointe for the Southern District of Florida said in a statement that a tenth of a gram of fentanyl, about the size of a small pinch of salt, was enough to kill Eller. Lapointe said the sentence reflects that Guerrero sold the fentanyl that killed his friend and was caught carrying more fentanyl for distribution just two days later.

Guerrero's extensive criminal history included documented gang membership and prior convictions for attempted robbery with a firearm in California, aggravated assault in Georgia, and cocaine and fentanyl possession offenses in Florida. Federal prosecutors said they will trace fatal doses back to the dealers who sold them and hold those dealers fully accountable.

hero.headline: 86-year-old woman dies after crash at Port St. Lucie intersection
hero.body:
An 86-year-old woman died Thursday after failing to yield at a Port St. Lucie intersection and being struck by an SUV driven by a 17-year-old boy. Marie R. Martin was driving a 2006 Hyundai Elantra west on Southwest Lawndale Avenue when she entered the intersection with Southwest Savona Boulevard from near a stop sign and failed to yield to a northbound 2026 Honda HR-V at approximately 2:30 p.m.

The Honda struck the driver's side of Martin's Hyundai in a T-bone collision. The impact left the Hyundai off the roadway near a cluster of palm trees with visible damage to its driver's side. St. Lucie Fire Rescue extricated Martin from the Hyundai before transporting her to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital with critical injuries. She later died at the hospital despite efforts to save her. The 17-year-old driver of the Honda was not injured in the crash.

The Port St. Lucie Police Department's Traffic Homicide Unit continues to investigate the crash at the intersection east of Interstate 95. Body-camera video recorded after the crash shows Port St. Lucie police officers and St. Lucie County Fire District personnel at the scene, along with fire engines, rescue vehicles and traffic cones blocking part of the intersection.

cards.headline: Man accused of attacking convicted killer Otto Lenke in St. Lucie County Jail
cards.teaser: Robert Castro allegedly struck convicted murderer Otto Lenke in the face inside a jail dorm on July 6, knocking off his glasses and cutting his nose.
cards.body:
Robert Castro struck Otto Lenke in the face inside a St. Lucie County Jail dorm on July 6, knocking off his glasses and cutting the upper part of his nose, according to an arrest affidavit. A jail sergeant witnessed Castro strike Lenke, and surveillance video showed Castro approaching Lenke and hitting him in the face. Lenke told a detective he had been using a jail-issued tablet to watch a chess game when Castro attacked him.

Castro, 30, is charged with battery by a person detained in a prison or jail facility, a felony. The charge was filed July 20. When investigators attempted to interview Castro on July 16, he repeatedly stated that he did not understand his Miranda rights and did not want to speak with the detective, ending the interview.

Lenke, a former Melbourne police officer and Indian River County firefighter, was convicted in May of first-degree murder and first-degree arson in the 2021 death of Richard Benson. Castro was convicted in 2024 of first-degree murder with a firearm in the death of his former girlfriend, Taylor Ann Sato, but the Fourth District Court of Appeal reversed the conviction in February after finding that the trial court failed to properly complete the process for determining whether Castro was competent to stand trial.
cards.article_text: A man awaiting a possible retrial in the fatal shooting of his former girlfriend is accused of attacking convicted murderer Otto Lenke inside the St. According to an arrest affidavit, Robert Castro approached Lenke in a jail dorm on July 6 and struck him in the face, knocking off his glasses. Lenke approached an intercom and reported the attack to corrections staff, the affidavit says. A deputy noticed a cut on the upper part of Lenke’s nose, and a nurse treated the injury. A jail sergeant witnessed Castro strike Lenke, according to investigators. Surveillance video also showed Castro approaching Lenke and hitting him in the face, the affidavit says. Lenke later told a detective he had been using a jail-issued tablet to watch a chess game when Castro attacked him. Investigators attempted to interview Castro on July 16. The affidavit says Castro repeatedly stated that he did not understand his Miranda rights and did not want to speak with the detective, ending the interview. Castro, 30, is charged with battery by a person detained in a prison or jail facility, a felony. The new charge was filed July 20. Lenke, a former Melbourne police officer and Indian River County firefighter, was convicted in May of first-degree murder and first-degree arson in the 2021 death of Richard Benson. Prosecutors said Lenke shot Benson three times inside Benson’s Fort Pierce motorcycle shop, poured an accelerant on him and set him on fire while he was still alive. A jury later voted 11-1 to recommend that Lenke be sentenced to death. Castro’s murder conviction reversed Castro was convicted in 2024 of first-degree murder with a firearm in the death of his former girlfriend, Taylor Ann Sato, and sentenced to life in prison. However, the Fourth District Court of Appeal reversed the conviction in February after finding that the trial court failed to properly complete the process for determining whether Castro was competent to stand trial. A psychologist found Castro competent in November 2022. Five days later, his attorneys raised concerns about his condition, and the original judge said Castro had definitely decompensated before ordering another evaluation. The appeals court said the record contained no additional evaluation, report or competency hearing after that order. Nearly two years later, a different judge declared Castro competent based on the original 2022 evaluation. Castro then went to trial and was convicted. The appellate court ruled that a two-year-old evaluation was not sufficient because competency must be assessed close to the time of trial. The case was sent back to the trial court to determine whether Castro’s competency during the 2024 trial can now be reliably evaluated. Castro would receive a new trial if a retrospective evaluation cannot be conducted or if the court determines he was not competent during the original trial. 2022 killing Fort Pierce police accused Castro of killing Sato outside her Timber Ridge Lane home during the early morning hours of July 23, 2022. According to the original arrest affidavit, a man called 911 and said he had shot and killed his girlfriend and was considering killing himself. Officers arrived and found Sato outside the home with multiple gunshot wounds. Investigators reported finding six gunshot wounds and several 9 mm shell casings near her body. Sato’s stepfather told detectives that she and Castro had recently ended a long-term relationship. He said Sato had blocked Castro’s phone number, but Castro continued trying to contact her by sending repeated $1 transactions through Cash App with messages attached. The stepfather also told police Castro had previously threatened to kill Sato. After listening to part of the 911 call, he identified the caller’s voice as Castro’s, according to the affidavit. Castro later surrendered to deputies in St. Investigators said several rounds of 9 mm ammunition were found in his pocket. His police interview ended after an attorney arrived and directed detectives not to question him further.

U.S. District Judge Aileen Cannon imposed the sentence after a federal jury convicted Guerrero in May 2026 of conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute fentanyl resulting in death and distribution of fentanyl resulting in death.

Guerrero sold fentanyl in Indian River County on May 16, 2023, exchanging 0.1 gram of the drug for another controlled substance known as molly. The drug transaction was captured on a doorbell camera. Hours later, David Eller was found dead inside his Vero Beach home. Investigators recovered drug paraphernalia, including a small piece of burnt aluminum foil that Eller used to receive the fentanyl from Guerrero on the victim's front porch, near his body.

Two days later, on May 18, 2023, Guerrero was arrested and found in possession of additional quantities of fentanyl intended for distribution. U.S. Attorney Markenzy Lapointe for the Southern District of Florida said a tenth of a gram of fentanyl, about the size of a small pinch of salt, was enough to kill Eller. Lapointe said the case was not a small drug deal and that Guerrero sold the fentanyl that killed his friend and was caught carrying more fentanyl for distribution just two days later.

Guerrero's extensive criminal history included documented gang membership and prior convictions for attempted robbery with a firearm in California, aggravated assault in Georgia, and cocaine and fentanyl possession offenses in Florida. Federal prosecutors said they worked with the DEA and local law enforcement partners to trace the fatal dose back to the dealer and hold him fully accountable.

cards.headline: Inmate awaiting retrial charged with attacking convicted killer Otto Lenke at St. Lucie County Jail
cards.teaser: Robert Castro, 30, attacked convicted murderer Otto Lenke inside a St. Lucie County Jail dorm on July 6, knocking off his glasses and cutting his nose.
cards.body:
Robert Castro approached Otto Lenke in a St. Lucie County Jail dorm on July 6 and struck him in the face, knocking off his glasses, according to an arrest affidavit. Lenke approached an intercom and reported the attack to corrections staff. A deputy noticed a cut on the upper part of Lenke's nose, and a nurse treated the injury. A jail sergeant witnessed Castro strike Lenke, and surveillance video showed Castro approaching Lenke and hitting him in the face.

Castro is charged with battery by a person detained in a prison or jail facility, a felony. The new charge was filed July 20. Lenke, a former Melbourne police officer and Indian River County firefighter, was convicted in May of first-degree murder and first-degree arson in the 2021 death of Richard Benson. Prosecutors said Lenke shot Benson three times inside Benson's Fort Pierce motorcycle shop, poured an accelerant on him and set him on fire while he was still alive.

Castro was convicted in 2024 of first-degree murder with a firearm in the death of his former girlfriend, Taylor Ann Sato, and sentenced to life in prison. However, the Fourth District Court of Appeal reversed the conviction in February after finding that the trial court failed to properly complete the process for determining whether Castro was competent to stand trial. The case was sent back to the trial court to determine whether Castro's competency during the 2024 trial can now be reliably evaluated.
cards.article_text: A man awaiting a possible retrial in the fatal shooting of his former girlfriend is accused of attacking convicted murderer Otto Lenke inside the St. According to an arrest affidavit, Robert Castro approached Lenke in a jail dorm on July 6 and struck him in the face, knocking off his glasses. Lenke approached an intercom and reported the attack to corrections staff, the affidavit says. A deputy noticed a cut on the upper part of Lenke’s nose, and a nurse treated the injury. A jail sergeant witnessed Castro strike Lenke, according to investigators. Surveillance video also showed Castro approaching Lenke and hitting him in the face, the affidavit says. Lenke later told a detective he had been using a jail-issued tablet to watch a chess game when Castro attacked him. Investigators attempted to interview Castro on July 16. The affidavit says Castro repeatedly stated that he did not understand his Miranda rights and did not want to speak with the detective, ending the interview. Castro, 30, is charged with battery by a person detained in a prison or jail facility, a felony. The new charge was filed July 20. Lenke, a former Melbourne police officer and Indian River County firefighter, was convicted in May of first-degree murder and first-degree arson in the 2021 death of Richard Benson. Prosecutors said Lenke shot Benson three times inside Benson’s Fort Pierce motorcycle shop, poured an accelerant on him and set him on fire while he was still alive. A jury later voted 11-1 to recommend that Lenke be sentenced to death. Castro’s murder conviction reversed Castro was convicted in 2024 of first-degree murder with a firearm in the death of his former girlfriend, Taylor Ann Sato, and sentenced to life in prison. However, the Fourth District Court of Appeal reversed the conviction in February after finding that the trial court failed to properly complete the process for determining whether Castro was competent to stand trial. A psychologist found Castro competent in November 2022. Five days later, his attorneys raised concerns about his condition, and the original judge said Castro had definitely decompensated before ordering another evaluation. The appeals court said the record contained no additional evaluation, report or competency hearing after that order. Nearly two years later, a different judge declared Castro competent based on the original 2022 evaluation. Castro then went to trial and was convicted. The appellate court ruled that a two-year-old evaluation was not sufficient because competency must be assessed close to the time of trial. The case was sent back to the trial court to determine whether Castro’s competency during the 2024 trial can now be reliably evaluated. Castro would receive a new trial if a retrospective evaluation cannot be conducted or if the court determines he was not competent during the original trial. 2022 killing Fort Pierce police accused Castro of killing Sato outside her Timber Ridge Lane home during the early morning hours of July 23, 2022. According to the original arrest affidavit, a man called 911 and said he had shot and killed his girlfriend and was considering killing himself. Officers arrived and found Sato outside the home with multiple gunshot wounds. Investigators reported finding six gunshot wounds and several 9 mm shell casings near her body. Sato’s stepfather told detectives that she and Castro had recently ended a long-term relationship. He said Sato had blocked Castro’s phone number, but Castro continued trying to contact her by sending repeated $1 transactions through Cash App with messages attached. The stepfather also told police Castro had previously threatened to kill Sato. After listening to part of the 911 call, he identified the caller’s voice as Castro’s, according to the affidavit. Castro later surrendered to deputies in St. Investigators said several rounds of 9 mm ammunition were found in his pocket. His police interview ended after an attorney arrived and directed detectives not to question him further.

hero.headline: 86-year-old woman dies after Port St. Lucie intersection crash
hero.body:
Marie R. Martin, 86, died Thursday after her Hyundai Elantra was struck at the intersection of Southwest Savona Boulevard and Southwest Lawndale Avenue in Port St. Lucie. Port St. Lucie Police Department officers responded to the crash at approximately 2:30 p.m.

The preliminary investigation indicates Martin was driving a 2006 Hyundai Elantra westbound on Southwest Lawndale Avenue when she entered the intersection from near a stop sign and failed to yield the right of way to a northbound 2026 Honda HR-V driven by a 17-year-old boy. The Honda struck the driver's side of the Hyundai, causing the Honda to T-bone Martin's vehicle.

St. Lucie Fire Rescue extricated Martin from the Hyundai before transporting her to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital with critical injuries. She later died at the hospital. Body camera video recorded after the crash shows the Hyundai off the roadway near a cluster of palm trees with visible damage to its driver's side and emergency crews working around the vehicle. The Honda came to rest on the grass nearby, close to vegetation and a roadside sign.

The 17-year-old driver of the Honda was not injured in the crash. The Port St. Lucie Police Department Traffic Homicide Unit continues to investigate the crash. The intersection is located east of Interstate 95.

Officers responded at approximately 2:30 p.m. Thursday at the intersection of Southwest Savona Boulevard and Southwest Lawndale Avenue, east of Interstate 95. The preliminary investigation indicates that a 2026 Honda HR-V, driven by a 17-year-old boy, was traveling northbound on Southwest Savona Boulevard approaching the intersection with SW Lawndale Avenue. A 2006 Hyundai Elantra, driven by Marie R. Martin, was traveling westbound near the stop sign on Southwest Lawndale Avenue. Investigators determined that Martin entered the intersection and failed to yield the right-of-way to the northbound Honda, resulting in the Honda striking the driver's side of the Hyundai. This caused the Honda to T-bone the Hyundai. Martin was extricated by St. Lucie Fire Rescue and was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital with critical injuries. Martin later succumbed to her injuries. The 17-year-old driver was not injured in the crash. Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

cards.headline: King's Landing development in Fort Pierce nears completion of first luxury villas
cards.teaser: Construction is advancing on the King's Landing development project in downtown Fort Pierce, with nearly two residences sold and multiple villas nearing completion.
cards.body:
The King's Landing development project in downtown Fort Pierce is advancing with construction milestones. Brooke Harris, Team Lead of the Beachfront Brooke Team powered by Keller Williams Realty, said they are almost done with Villas 9 and 10, and the foundation has been laid for Villas 7 and 8. Two residences have been sold and are nearing completion.

The project features ten luxury villas, condos, retail spaces, restaurants, a parking garage, and a Marriott Hotel, which has signed an agreement for the development. The project is located in the waterfront district near the city marina and historic downtown. Harris said the location gives residents a walkability factor to go down to shopping, restaurants, retail, and the marina for boat storage.

Michelle Chaffee Cavalcanti, executive director of Main Street Fort Pierce, said the development has the potential to have a lot of impact on local businesses by bringing in visitors and giving local families somewhere for family members to stay when they visit. Officials said the estimated completion date is November 2029.

The project features ten luxury villas, condos, retail spaces, restaurants, a parking garage, and a hotel. hero.headline: Los Angeles man sentenced to life in prison for fentanyl sale that killed Vero Beach resident
hero.body:
A federal judge sentenced a Los Angeles man to life in prison for selling fentanyl that caused the death of a Vero Beach resident and then trafficking the drug two days later. U.S. District Judge Aileen Cannon imposed the sentence on Alfonso Guerrero, 39, of Los Angeles, after a federal jury convicted him in May 2026 of conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute fentanyl resulting in death and distribution of fentanyl resulting in death.

On May 16, 2023, Guerrero sold 0.1 gram of fentanyl, commonly known as a point, in exchange for another controlled substance known as molly in Indian River County. The transaction was captured on a doorbell camera. Hours later, David Eller was found dead inside his Vero Beach home. Investigators recovered drug paraphernalia, including a small piece of burnt aluminum foil that Eller used to receive the fentanyl from Guerrero on his front porch, near his body.

Two days later, on May 18, 2023, Guerrero was arrested and found in possession of additional quantities of fentanyl intended for distribution. U.S. Attorney Markenzy Lapointe for the Southern District of Florida said a tenth of a gram of fentanyl, about the size of a small pinch of salt, was enough to kill Eller. The prosecutor emphasized that Guerrero sold the fentanyl that killed his friend and just two days later was caught carrying more fentanil for distribution.

Guerrero's criminal history included documented gang membership and prior convictions for attempted robbery with a firearm in California, aggravated assault in Georgia, and cocaine and fentanyl possession offenses in Florida. Federal prosecutors said the life sentence reflects the consequence of his deadly conduct and his long record of violence and crime.

hero.headline: Stuart man jailed after fleeing traffic stop, leading police chase into Martin County
hero.body:
David Allen Kingsley Jr., 31, was arrested July 28 after fleeing a Stuart Police officer during a traffic stop and leading law enforcement on a chase that ended in Martin County with assistance from the Martin County Sheriff's Office and Florida Highway Patrol. Kingsley remains in the Martin County Jail on a $40,000 bond.

A Stuart Police officer stopped Kingsley on an equipment violation the evening of July 28. After the officer discovered that Kingsley's driver's license was revoked, Kingsley took off. Kingsley led officers on a brief pursuit within the City of Stuart, striking another vehicle before continuing out of the city.

Kingsley continued driving recklessly into Martin County jurisdiction, where deputies with the Martin County Sheriff's Office and troopers with the Florida Highway Patrol assisted in the pursuit. The vehicle was ultimately stopped, and Kingsley surrendered without further incident.

Kingsley was charged with two counts of fleeing eluding law enforcement, one count of leaving the scene of a crash involving property damage, failure to obey an officer's order to stop, reckless driving, and driving while license suspended or revoked. He was in the Martin County Jail as of July 30 on those charges.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware named Florida State League Pitcher of the Week
hero.body:
St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware has been named the Florida State League Pitcher of the Week for the week of July 20-26, Minor League Baseball announced. Ware made two appearances at Clover Park against Fort Myers, one start on Tuesday and one relief outing on Sunday.

The southpaw pitched 7.0 scoreless innings across both games. He scattered three hits, walked two and struck out 12. The Mets won both games with Ware getting credit for the win on Sunday.

Ware, 22, was drafted by the Mets in the 15th round out of LSU in 2025. He made his pro debut with St. Lucie in April and has been with the team all season.

This is the first FSL Pitcher or Player of the Week award for the Mets this season.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast renters face high costs as rental market holds flat
cards.teaser: Renters across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties say the cost of living is putting a strain on their finances, while a local real estate agent reports the rental market has leveled off.
cards.body:
Renters on the Treasure Coast say the cost of living is putting a strain on their finances. Jesse Espinoza, a renter in Martin County, said the price of rent is taking a toll on his ability to afford basic expenses including food and pet care. A resident identified as Mike said his rent has gone up significantly since he first moved to the area, now three times more expensive than when he arrived.

Kelley Decowski, a real estate agent in Martin County, said the rental market is currently flat. Rental rates are not skyrocketing, but they are not coming down either. Martin County has the highest average rental rates on the Treasure Coast, ranging from $2,300 to $2,500 a month across all unit types. Indian River County has the lowest average rents in the region, ranging from $1,650 to $2,200 a month. St. Lucie County averages between $2,100 to $2,300 a month.

Decowski said more rental inventory is coming to the market, which could push prices down, though inflation remains a wildcard. She said prices may come down because of that inventory hitting the market, but price growth cannot be ruled out with inflationary pressures. Mike said everywhere in Florida is expensive, and renters are paying to play in the current market.

You have pets, I mean, it's almost impossible," Espinoza said.A resident identified as Mike said his rent has gone up significantly since he first moved to the area."It's three times more expensive than it was when I first moved down here," Mike said.Still, Mike said the Treasure Coast offers some relief compared to South Florida."If you're comparing it to Palm Beach or Miami, it's a discount," Mike said.That relative affordability is part of what drew Hunter to Martin County after growing up in Palm Beach Gardens."Affordability and rent prices are a little bit cheaper," Hunter said.Mike, however, said the difference is not dramatic."It might be a little bit cheaper in the Treasure Coast, but we're only talking a couple hundred bucks," Mike said.Kelley Decowski, a real estate agent in Martin County, said the rental market is currently flat."We're not seeing rental rates skyrocketing, but they're not really coming down either," Decowski said.Martin County is seeing the highest average rental rates on the Treasure Coast, ranging from $2,300 to $2,500 a month across all unit types. hero.headline: 86-year-old woman dies after Port St. Lucie intersection crash
hero.body:
An 86-year-old woman died Thursday after she pulled into the path of an SUV at a Port St. Lucie intersection and was struck. The crash happened at about 2:30 p.m. at Southwest Savona Boulevard and Southwest Lawndale Avenue.

Marie R. Martin was driving a 2006 Hyundai Elantra west on Lawndale Avenue when she entered the intersection from near a stop sign and failed to yield to a northbound 2026 Honda HR-V. The Honda, driven by a 17-year-old boy, struck the drivers side of Martins car. Body-camera video recorded after the crash shows the Hyundai off the roadway near a cluster of palm trees, with visible damage to its drivers side and emergency crews working around the vehicle. The Honda also came to rest on the grass nearby, close to vegetation and a roadside sign.

Martin had to be extricated from the Hyundai before she was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital with critical injuries. She later died despite efforts to save her. The teenage driver of the Honda was not injured.

The Port St. Lucie Police Departments Traffic Homicide Unit continues to investigate the crash. Debris and emergency equipment were scattered across the grass between the two vehicles.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office seeks 'Flamingo Bandit' after home burglarized twice
cards.teaser: A suspected burglar wearing a tropical shirt with a giant pink flamingo burglarized a St. Lucie County home twice in one day.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriffs Office is searching for a man photographed wearing a tropical shirt dominated by a giant pink flamingo. The suspect, now known as the Flamingo Bandit, is accused of burglarizing a residence twice on July 28.

Investigators said the suspect entered a residence on July 28 and stole a laptop, miscellaneous food and a key to the home. Deputies allege he then returned later that same day and used the stolen key to get inside a second time. The sheriffs office shared an image of the flamboyantly dressed suspect, hoping his difficult-to-miss wardrobe will help someone identify him.

Anyone who recognizes the man or has information about the case is asked to call the St. Lucie County Sheriffs Office at 772-462-7300 or email Deputy V. Ancewicz at PatrolTips@stluciesheriff.com.

hero.headline: Byron Donalds holds commanding lead in Florida GOP governor's race with three weeks until primary
hero.body:
U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds maintains a dominant position in Florida's Republican gubernatorial primary with fewer than three weeks remaining before the Aug. 19 election, buoyed by President Donald Trump's endorsement, superior name recognition and a significant financial advantage over his three main rivals. A political committee supporting Donalds this week released a statewide television and digital ad centered on affordability, showing Donalds playing basketball with his sons while promising to cut property taxes, lower insurance rates and reduce housing costs.

A public Cygnal survey conducted July 12-13 found Donalds leading with 43 percent, followed by investor James Fishback at 12 percent, Lt. Gov. Jay Collins at 11 percent and former House Speaker Paul Renner at 2 percent. Another 31 percent remained undecided. The survey included 500 likely Republican primary voters and had a margin of error of 4.38 percentage points. Collins' campaign released an internal poll this week showing a closer contest, with Donalds at 46 percent and Collins at 30 percent, though public polling has generally shown Collins much farther behind.

Fishback won a courtroom victory this week after Leon County Circuit Judge David Frank rejected Collins' attempt to remove him from the ballot. Collins had pointed to Fishback's 2020 vote in Washington, D.C., his purchase of a condominium there and tax, mortgage and homestead records as evidence that Fishback had established residency outside Florida. Frank ruled that Collins failed to overcome Florida's legal presumptions favoring continued residency and candidate access to the ballot. Fishback responded by calling on Collins to resign as lieutenant governor, calling the legal challenge an attempt to rig the election. Collins dismissed the demand and said his team had not yet decided whether to appeal.

Renner is using his closing campaign ads to emphasize his record as House speaker, including the expansion of school-choice programs and conservative legislation passed while he led the chamber. Vote-by-mail ballots have already been distributed for the Aug. 19 primary. Florida's mandatory early-voting period begins Aug. 8 and continues through Aug. 15, though counties may offer additional days. On the Democratic side, David Jolly is already focusing his attacks on Donalds, this week promising to halt new AI data-center construction until Florida develops stronger protections for its water supply, electric grid, communities and consumer privacy.

Jay Collins and investor James Fishback.University of South Florida political scientist Susan MacManus said the basic shape of the race has changed little. "This was about rigging an election."Collins dismissed the demand and criticized the ruling on Thursday."I think that his decision has basically put us in a position where, if you identify as a Floridian, you are a Floridian," Collins said. cards.headline: Judge rejects effort to remove James Fishback from Florida governor's race ballot
cards.teaser: Leon County Circuit Judge David Frank ruled that Lt. Gov. Jay Collins failed to prove investor James Fishback had abandoned his Florida residency, keeping Fishback in the Republican gubernatorial primary.
cards.body:
Leon County Circuit Judge David Frank rejected Lt. Gov. Jay Collins' attempt to remove investor James Fishback from the Republican gubernatorial primary ballot, ruling that Collins failed to overcome Florida's legal presumptions favoring continued residency and candidate access to the ballot. Florida's Constitution requires a candidate for governor to have lived in the state for the seven years preceding the election. Collins pointed to Fishback's 2020 vote in Washington, D.C., his purchase of a condominium there and tax, mortgage and homestead records as evidence that Fishback had established residency outside Florida.

Fishback maintained that he never intended to abandon his Florida residency. After the ruling, Fishback called on Collins to resign as lieutenant governor, saying the legal challenge was not about election integrity but about rigging an election. Collins dismissed the demand and criticized the ruling, saying his team had not yet made a final decision on whether to appeal.

The decision allows Fishback to remain on the Aug. 19 Republican primary ballot, where he trails frontrunner Byron Donalds. A public Cygnal survey conducted July 12-13 found Fishback at 12 percent support, trailing Donalds' 43 percent.

cards.headline: Paul Renner criticizes Anthony Fauci over China coronavirus research funding in Florida governor's race
cards.teaser: Former House Speaker Paul Renner escalated his criticism of Dr. Anthony Fauci, alleging the former federal infectious-disease official helped direct taxpayer money to coronavirus research in China that Renner believes led to the pandemic.
cards.body:
Former House Speaker Paul Renner, a candidate in Florida's Republican gubernatorial primary, alleged that Dr. Anthony Fauci helped direct taxpayer money for gain-of-function research in China, calling it potentially traitorous. Federal audits confirm that National Institutes of Health grants to the nonprofit EcoHealth Alliance included subawards involving the Wuhan Institute of Virology. The Department of Health and Human Services' inspector general found significant failures in NIH and EcoHealth's oversight of the grants, but its audit did not conclude that the research created SARS-CoV-2 or caused the pandemic.

The origin of the virus remains unresolved. The World Health Organization said the weight of available scientific evidence favors an animal-to-human spillover, either directly from bats or through another animal.

Renner is using his closing campaign ads to emphasize his record as House speaker, including the expansion of school-choice programs and conservative legislation passed while he led the chamber. A public Cygnal survey conducted July 12-13 found Renner at 2 percent support in the Republican primary, trailing frontrunner Byron Donalds' 43 percent.

cards.headline: David Jolly promises to halt new AI data centers in Florida until stronger protections are in place
cards.teaser: Democratic gubernatorial candidate David Jolly pledged to halt new AI data-center construction until Florida develops stronger protections for its water supply, electric grid, communities and consumer privacy.
cards.body:
Democratic gubernatorial candidate David Jolly this week promised to halt new AI data-center construction until Florida develops stronger protections for its water supply, electric grid, communities and consumer privacy. Jolly's campaign also accused Republican frontrunner Byron Donalds of being too closely aligned with the data-center industry, pointing to millions of dollars in support it says came from interests connected to data-center development.

Donalds has argued Florida should embrace data centers while imposing protections for residents. He recently introduced federal legislation that would require the facilities to secure electricity and water from private sources instead of relying on public utility systems. The proposal is intended to prevent data centers from raising residential utility costs.

Jolly is focusing his attacks on Donalds ahead of the Aug. 19 primary, when Donalds is expected to secure the Republican nomination. A public Cygnal survey conducted July 12-13 found Donalds leading the Republican field with 43 percent support.

cards.headline: Florida gubernatorial candidates split on party allegiance as primary approaches
cards.teaser: University of South Florida political scientist Susan MacManus said the basic shape of Florida's Republican gubernatorial race has changed little, with Byron Donalds' three leading challengers remaining divided.
cards.body:
University of South Florida political scientist Susan MacManus said the basic shape of Florida's Republican gubernatorial race has changed little, with Donalds' three leading challengers remaining divided, making it more difficult for any one of them to consolidate the opposition. MacManus said Donalds' support has remained particularly durable among the highly partisan voters most likely to participate in a Republican primary.

hero.headline: Back-to-school bash in Port St. Lucie to feature free supplies, music and entertainment Saturday
hero.body:
A back-to-school bash on the Treasure Coast will feature free backpacks, school supplies, music, food, games, and a special guest appearance at 7 p.m. Saturday at MIDFLORIDA Credit Union Event Center in Port St. Lucie. The event takes place at 9221 S.E. Event Center Place starting at 3 p.m.

The event is free and offers families throughout St. Lucie County an opportunity to prepare for the upcoming school year while children participate in games and activities. Backpacks and school supplies will be available while supplies last.

The back-to-school bash is among several community events scheduled for the weekend across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Other local activities include Unity Fest in Delray Beach and multiple farmers markets and art walks in West Palm Beach.

Families can find more information about the Port St. Lucie event and other weekend activities throughout the region by visiting local event calendars and community websites.

cards.teaser: Earl's Hideaway Lounge and Tiki Bar in Sebastian will feature performances including Rezen8 Band, Swamp Dawgs and Petty USA throughout the next month.
cards.body:
Earl's Hideaway Lounge Tiki Bar at 1405 Indian River Drive in Sebastian will host live music acts through Aug. 30. Additional acts scheduled throughout August include tribute bands Hair Peace, Hairdaze and Petty USA. Other performers include Midnight Johnny, Element 7, Hi Mileage, Bar Fly, Rebel Soul, Luna Pearl, Jerzi Band, Triple Shot, Phoenix Band and Eddie Leighton Project. Most performances are scheduled for Thursday, Friday, Saturday or Sunday.

Ticket information and a full schedule are available at earlshideaway.com.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Museum of Art features American artists, new building exhibit through 2027
cards.teaser: More than 80 works by artists including Benjamin West, John Singer Sargent and Mary Cassatt are on display at Vero Beach Museum of Art through Aug. 16.
cards.body:
An exhibition titled American Made at Vero Beach Museum of Art includes more than 80 works by artists including Benjamin West, Sarah Miriam Peale, Edward Moran, John Singer Sargent, Mary Cassatt, Robert Henri and Charles Alston. The exhibit runs through Aug. 16 at the Holmes and Titelman Galleries at 3001 Riverside Park Drive in Vero Beach.

Another exhibit, James Prosek: At Work, is on display at the museum's Holmes Gallery through Oct. 25. The exhibit features projects which define the artist's first 30 years of artmaking. Admission is free to members, children 17 and younger, and military veterans and active duty military with valid ID. Admission is $12 for adults, $11 for seniors and $5 for students with ID.

The museum is also displaying Envisioning the New VBMA, an exhibit tracing the evolution of designs for the museum's new building and transformed campus created by Allied Works architecture and Unknown Studio Landscape Architecture Urban Design. That exhibit runs through Jan. 3, 2027.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware named Florida State League Pitcher of the Week
hero.body:
St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware has been named the Florida State League Pitcher of the Week for the week of July 20-26, Minor League Baseball announced. Ware made two appearances last week at Clover Park against Fort Myers, one start on Tuesday and one relief outing on Sunday.

The southpaw combined to pitch 7.0 scoreless innings. He scattered three hits, walked two and struck out 12. The Mets won both games with Ware getting credit for the win on Sunday.

Ware, 22, was drafted by the Mets in the 15th round out of LSU in 2025. He made his pro debut with St. Lucie in April and has been with the team all season.

This is the first FSL Pitcher or Player of the Week award for the Mets this season. The St. Lucie Mets play their home games at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast rental costs strain residents as Martin County averages $2,300 to $2,500 monthly
hero.body:
Renters across the Treasure Coast say high costs are straining their finances, with Martin County showing the highest average rental rates in the region at $2,300 to $2,500 a month across all unit types. Kelley Decowski, a real estate agent in Martin County, said the rental market is currently flat, with rates neither rising nor falling.

Jesse Espinoza, a Martin County renter, said the price of rent is taking a toll. A resident identified as Mike said his rent has gone up significantly since he first moved to the area. Mike said his rent is three times more expensive than when he first moved to the Treasure Coast. Hunter, who moved to Martin County from Palm Beach Gardens, cited affordability and rent prices as reasons for relocating. Mike said the difference between the Treasure Coast and South Florida is not dramatic, noting the Treasure Coast might be a couple hundred dollars cheaper.

Indian River County has the lowest average rents in the region, ranging from $1,650 to $2,200 a month. St. Lucie County averages between $2,100 to $2,300 a month. Martin County averages reflect a wide range of properties, from luxury and waterfront listings and private homes to apartment complexes, Decowski said.

Decowski said more rental inventory is coming to the market, which could push prices down, though inflation remains a wildcard. Mike said everywhere in Florida is expensive. Despite the costs, Mike said he has accepted the reality of renting in the current market.

hero.headline: Inmate awaiting retrial for Fort Pierce murder charged with attacking convicted killer in St. Lucie County Jail
hero.body:
Robert Castro, 30, attacked convicted murderer Otto Lenke inside a St. Lucie County Jail dorm on July 6, knocking off his glasses and cutting his nose, according to an arrest affidavit filed July 20. Castro is awaiting a possible retrial in the fatal shooting of his former girlfriend, Taylor Ann Sato, outside her Timber Ridge Lane home in Fort Pierce in 2022.

A jail sergeant witnessed Castro strike Lenke in the face, and surveillance video captured the attack. Lenke told a detective he had been using a jail-issued tablet to watch a chess game when Castro approached and hit him. A deputy noticed a cut on the upper part of Lenke's nose, and a nurse treated the injury. Castro refused to speak with investigators on July 16, repeatedly stating he did not understand his Miranda rights. He is now charged with battery by a person detained in a prison or jail facility, a felony.

Lenke, a former Melbourne police officer and Indian River County firefighter, was convicted in May of first-degree murder and first-degree arson in the 2021 death of Richard Benson. Prosecutors said Lenke shot Benson three times inside Benson's Fort Pierce motorcycle shop, poured an accelerant on him and set him on fire while he was still alive. A jury voted 11-1 to recommend that Lenke be sentenced to death.

Castro was convicted in 2024 of first-degree murder with a firearm in the death of Sato and sentenced to life in prison. The Fourth District Court of Appeal reversed his conviction in February after finding the trial court failed to properly complete the process for determining whether Castro was competent to stand trial. The appellate court ruled that a two-year-old evaluation was not sufficient because competency must be assessed close to the time of trial. The case was sent back to the trial court to determine whether Castro's competency during the 2024 trial can now be reliably evaluated. Castro would receive a new trial if a retrospective evaluation cannot be conducted or if the court determines he was not competent during the original trial.

However, the Fourth District Court of Appeal reversed the conviction in February after finding that the trial court failed to properly complete the process for determining whether Castro was competent to stand trial. A psychologist found Castro competent in November 2022. Five days later, his attorneys raised concerns about his condition, and the original judge said Castro had definitely decompensated before ordering another evaluation. The appeals court said the record contained no additional evaluation, report or competency hearing after that order. According to the original arrest affidavit, a man called 911 and said he had shot and killed his girlfriend and was considering killing himself. Officers arrived and found Sato outside the home with multiple gunshot wounds. Investigators reported finding six gunshot wounds and several 9 mm shell casings near her body. Sato’s stepfather told detectives that she and Castro had recently ended a long-term relationship. cards.headline: Los Angeles man sentenced to life in prison for fentanyl sale that killed Vero Beach resident
cards.teaser: Alfonso Guerrero, 39, sold fentanyl that killed David Eller at his Vero Beach home in May 2023, then was caught carrying more fentanyl for distribution two days later.
cards.body:
U.S. District Judge Aileen Cannon sentenced Alfonso Guerrero, 39, of Los Angeles, to life in federal prison after a federal jury convicted him in May 2026 of conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute fentanyl resulting in death and distribution of fentanyl resulting in death. Guerrero sold fentanyl in Indian River County on May 16, 2023, exchanging 0.1 gram of fentanyl for another controlled substance known as molly. The drug transaction was captured on a doorbell camera. Hours later, Eller was found dead inside his Vero Beach home.

Investigators recovered drug paraphernalia, including a small piece of burnt aluminum foil that Eller used to receive the fentanyl from Guerrero on his front porch, near his body. Two days later, on May 18, 2023, Guerrero was arrested and found in possession of additional quantities of fentanyl intended for distribution.

Guerrero's extensive criminal history included documented gang membership and prior convictions for attempted robbery with a firearm in California, aggravated assault in Georgia, and cocaine and fentanyl possession offenses in Florida. U.S. Attorney Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida said a tenth of a gram of fentanyl, about the size of a small pinch of salt, was enough to kill Eller.

"This was not a small drug deal. Guerrero sold the fentanyl that killed his friend and, just two days later, was caught carrying more fentanyl for distribution. Officials said the drug transaction was captured on a doorbell camera. Hours later, Eller was found dead inside his Vero Beach home. Investigators recovered drug paraphernalia, including a small piece of burnt aluminum foil that the victim used to receive the fentanyl from Guerrero on the victim's front porch, near his body. Two days later, on May 18, 2023, prosecutors said Guerrero was arrested and found in possession of additional quantities of fentanyl intended for distribution. cards.headline: Fort Pierce police failed to arrest man before he killed Taylor Ann Sato outside Timber Ridge Lane home, internal investigation finds
cards.teaser: Robert Castro killed his former girlfriend Taylor Ann Sato outside her Fort Pierce home in July 2022, months after police accused Detective Louis Potter of failing to thoroughly investigate rape and assault allegations against Castro.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce police accused Castro of killing Sato outside her Timber Ridge Lane home during the early morning hours of July 23, 2022. A man called 911 and said he had shot and killed his girlfriend and was considering killing himself. Officers arrived and found Sato outside the home with multiple gunshot wounds. Investigators reported finding six gunshot wounds and several 9 mm shell casings near her body.

Kelly Matthews, Wilson's former girlfriend, told WPTV she reported to law enforcement in February 2019 that Wilson had beaten, kidnapped and raped her. Matthews said she had begged Detective Louis Potter to arrest him. Potter collected Wilson's DNA but 34 days later closed the case before the lab results came back. In his report, Potter wrote there were no witnesses, no evidence, and that Wilson denied the allegations, concluding there was no probable cause to make an arrest.

A Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office internal affairs investigation found Potter failed to conduct a thorough sex crimes investigation. Investigators concluded he closed the case before reviewing DNA results, and when those results came back confirming Wilson's DNA was found at the scene, Potter failed to follow up. The internal affairs report found Matthews' account was corroborated by her injuries and evidence collected from the vehicle where the alleged crimes occurred, including a pocket knife and torn clothing. Potter was suspended without pay for 120 hours and reassigned to administrative duties.
cards.article_text: A Netflix docuseries is drawing renewed national attention to a Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office detective who interviewed accused killer Wade Wilson — also known as the Deadpool Killer — months before Wilson murdered two women in 2019, sparking widespread calls for the detective's termination.WATCH WPTV's COVERAGE BELOW:The series has focused scrutiny on Detective Louis Potter, who investigated rape and assault allegations against Wilson in February 2019. An internal affairs investigation later found Potter failed to conduct a thorough sex crimes investigation — a conclusion that has fueled a public petition calling for his firing that has grown to more than 16,000 signatures.Wilson's former girlfriend, Kelly Matthews, told WPTV she reported to law enforcement that Wilson had beaten, kidnapped, and raped her. She described the injuries she says she suffered during the attack. "Ligature marks on my wrists and ankles, I had red marks around my neck, a bite mark on my cheek and my ear, a busted lip, bloody nose," Matthews said.Matthews said she sought medical attention and reported the attack to law enforcement within hours."I had begged the detective to arrest him. Literally just detain him, pick him up or whatever and he refused and then he told me after the fact that he had already met up with him and done DNA and stuff," Matthews said.Potter did collect Wilson's DNA. But according to PBSO records, 34 days later, he closed the case — before the lab results came back."He even agreed in his report that my injuries were consistent with my story but then he turned around and just closed everything," Matthews said.In his report, Potter wrote there were no witnesses, no evidence, and that Wilson denied the allegations, concluding there was no probable cause to make an arrest.The Netflix series drew widespread attention to Potter's tone during his interrogation of Wilson, with viewers questioning whether he was too quick to accept Wilson's denials.During the interrogation, Potter told Wilson: Wilson responded: Matthews said she did not know what Potter had said during that interrogation until she watched the Netflix documentary. "I didn't know he had said any of that stuff until I saw the documentary," she said.Just days after Wilson murdered two women in October 2019, WPTV sat down with Matthews, who described the earlier attack. Years later, after watching Wilson's murder trial, Matthews filed a complaint against Potter. "Had Detective Potter arrested my ex, he likely wouldn't have gone on to murder two women," Matthews wrote in the complaint.That complaint triggered an internal investigation.WPTV obtained a copy of that report. In the report it says PBSO investigators concluded Potter failed to conduct a thorough sex crimes investigation. They found he closed the case before reviewing DNA results, and when those results came back — confirming Wilson's DNA was found at the scene — Potter failed to follow up. Investigators also found he failed to seek an arrest for dating violence.The internal affairs report found Matthews' account was corroborated by her injuries and evidence collected from the vehicle where the alleged crimes occurred, including a pocket knife and torn clothing — all factors the report says point to probable cause.Former State Attorney Dave Aronberg, who was in office in 2019, said the case never landed on his desk. He called the outcome a tragedy."The Wade Wilson matter is just a tragedy, because there are so many steps, if things had gone a different direction, that perhaps these victims would still be alive," Aronberg said.When asked whether the case was mishandled, Aronberg urged caution about judging decisions in hindsight, but said his office would have taken a closer look had the case been referred. "You don't want to be a Monday morning quarterback, because we're looking at this with the perspective of hindsight," Aronberg said."Clearly she does appear to be very credible. The fact that he's had a rap sheet, he's done this before, that would have come into play at a variety of levels," Aronberg said.Over the phone, PBSO said detectives need probable cause before referring a case to the State Attorney's Office — evidence Potter claimed did not exist. But the internal affairs report found Matthews' account did have substantial probable cause.Aronberg said Potter's discipline may hinge on whether he was required to consult with the State Attorney's Office before closing the case."If he was required to consult with the State Attorney's Office before dropping a charge like this, then this would be a violation of that policy, and he has been sanctioned for violations," Aronberg said.WATCH WPTV's PREVIOUS COVERAGE:Potter was suspended without pay for 120 hours. In a statement, PBSO said Potter "used poor discretionary judgment in the handling of a criminal case without following established agency procedures," adding that he was reassigned to administrative duties and received appropriate discipline.Years after the alleged rape and the murders, Potter when questioned if he would change how he handled the case said no. Aronberg pushed back on that position. "I don't think it's helpful to say that you know nothing could have been done differently when clearly things could have," Aronberg said.Matthews raised broader concerns about what Potter's approach could mean for other potential victims."Who knows how many women he's done this to, or men. Because he even says in the report he would do it the same way like if anyone else had this happen," Matthews said.Since the series aired, Matthews said she feels a sense of relief that the full story is now public."Ever since the Netflix thing came out I feel like I can breathe and I'm like OK, everyone knows the truth, everything's out there," Matthews said.PBSO has said it will not fire Potter over renewed attention to the case. Potter plans to retire Friday, July 31, and has not responded to requests for comment.Matthews said the experience has left a lasting impact on her trust in law enforcement."I was always taught as a kid to go to law enforcement and trust them and it ended up tainting my trust in law enforcement for awhile, because these are supposed to be the people that are going to protect you and he didn't," Matthews said.Full statement from PBSO below:This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Our editorial team verifies all reporting on all platforms for fairness and accuracy.
